principles.statement: FM partitioning with greedy local search and random restarts achieves ~87 on Max-Cut (n<=1000, m<=20000) within a 1s time limit, outperforming trivial assignment by ~37 points.
principles.regime: Max-Cut with n<=1000, m<=20000, 1s time limit per test case
principles.mechanism: Greedy local search converges to a local optimum quickly. FM passes consider the full sequence of vertex flips and select the best prefix, enabling escape from local optima. Multiple restarts with different RNG seeds explore diverse regions of solution space.
principles.applicability_bounds: Holds for sparse graphs (m<=20000) where FM passes complete within the time budget. May not scale to much larger graphs where a single FM pass is too slow.

principles.statement: RNG-seed-dependent variance in FM+restarts can cause ~5-point score drops (81.5 vs 87.0), suggesting the algorithm's performance is sensitive to the number of restarts completed within the time budget.
principles.regime: Max-Cut with tight time limits (0.90s budget) and time-based RNG
principles.mechanism: With time-based seeds, some runs may spend more time on suboptimal initial partitions, leaving fewer restarts before the time limit. The variance suggests the restart count (not the algorithm quality) is the bottleneck.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies when using chrono-based seeds. Fixed seeds would eliminate this variance but reduce solution diversity.

principles.statement: Linear-cooling SA (T proportional to remaining time fraction, T0=3.0, 0.10s per restart) outperforms geometric-cooling SA (T*=0.9995) by ~1 point on Max-Cut (87.5 vs 86.6), because geometric cooling exhausts useful exploration in ~0.5ms while linear cooling uses the full restart budget.
principles.regime: Max-Cut with n<=1000, m<=20000, 1s time limit, greedy+SA+restarts framework
principles.mechanism: Geometric cooling (0.9995^k) drops temperature below 0.01 after ~10.6k iterations (~0.5ms), making the remaining ~0.4ms per restart equivalent to greedy. Linear cooling (T = T0*(1-t/budget)) ensures temperature scales from T0 to Tf across the full 0.10s SA phase, giving ~1.7M SA iterations of productive exploration per restart. Fewer but deeper restarts (9 vs 1000+) yield higher-quality cuts.
principles.applicability_bounds: Tested on competition-style Max-Cut instances. The optimal restart budget (0.10s) may differ on larger/denser graphs or different hardware speeds.

principles.statement: Linear-cooling SA with time-proportional restarts reduces RNG-seed variance from ~5 points (iter-1 FM+SA) to ~0.05 points (std 0.03), likely because the fixed 0.10s SA budget per restart is more deterministic than time-checked geometric cooling that races against the clock.
principles.mechanism: The batched time check (every 256 iterations) and fixed SA budget per restart make each restart's behavior more predictable across seeds. Geometric cooling with per-iteration time checks introduces more timing-dependent variance.
principles.applicability_bounds: Variance reduction observed on local hardware. Judge hardware variance may differ.

principles.statement: For Max-Cut (n≤1000, m≤20000) with incremental gain SA, restart budget allocation (depth vs breadth) does not affect score: 0.30s×3 restarts and 0.03s×30 restarts both achieve ~87.5 on the judge, indicating the solution landscape has many near-equivalent local optima reachable by either strategy.
principles.regime: Max-Cut, n≤1000, m≤20000, 0.90s total budget, linear cooling SA with incremental gain
principles.mechanism: Incremental gain tracking speeds SA iterations ~5x, but this does not raise the score ceiling because the quality bottleneck is not iteration count — it is the Max-Cut landscape structure. Random restarts (even shallow ones) reliably find optima near 87.5, so deeper per-restart exploration provides no additional benefit.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies to Max-Cut with the given size/density range. May not hold for larger graphs or sparser structures where deep exploration could find rarer, better optima.

principles.statement: The ~87.5 score ceiling on Max-Cut (problem 192) is robust across SA configurations: geometric cooling (86.6), linear cooling (87.5), incremental gain + long SA (87.5), incremental gain + short SA (87.6). Further SA optimization is unlikely to push significantly beyond this ceiling.
principles.regime: Max-Cut problem 192, judge evaluation, all SA variants tested across 3 iterations
principles.mechanism: Multiple SA configurations with varying iteration speed, cooling schedules, and restart budgets all converge to ~87.5. This suggests the score is bounded by the problem structure (graph properties, checker scoring function) rather than algorithmic configuration. Breaking through would require a fundamentally different approach (e.g., problem-specific graph decomposition, semidefinite relaxation, or multi-flip neighborhoods).
principles.applicability_bounds: Specific to problem 192 test cases and checker. Different test instances could have different ceilings.
